messages:
Anya: quick intake — proposing a small PRD to lock down "behavioral contracts" for model selection + fallback across hosted / dedicated / private. Problem: customers are seeing different outputs or silent fallbacks during capacity events which breaks their acceptance tests.

Anya: problem statement: 1) model variant selection should be deterministic given the same routing policy + pin; 2) fallback behavior must be explicit and discoverable by callers (reason codes, metadata); 3) rollout semantics must protect quality and latency.

Anya: MVP goals (short):
- define API-level contract for response metadata (model_variant, fallback_reason, request_id correlation)
- define acceptance metrics (latency targets, error rate ceilings, eval-suite deltas) and CI checks
- define a canary rollout recipe with automated gates and rollback triggers

Anya: MVP non-goals: console UI changes for pinning/routing, tenant self-serve routing rules, per-tenant cache tuning. Keep this API + infra only.

Sam: clarifying q — when you say deterministic, do you mean exact same model weights or just same variant family? also what's our latency target for the MVP?

Anya: not bitwise deterministic. We mean: given the same routing policy + pinned model version, the platform should choose the same serving variant (eg fp16-v1 vs int8-a) and expose which one was used. Latency target: p50 < 150ms for 512 tokens on Dedicated baseline; hosted may be higher.

Marta: customer note — Acme's compliance tests assert model identity and a short audit trail. They need a stable model_variant string and request_id correlation. Edge-case: tenant-specific prompt transforms may make outputs diverge even if the variant is the same.

Li: UX/API ask — include response metadata fields in the API response body and headers. Proposal: body includes {
  "model_variant": "string",
  "fallback_reason": "none | capacity | degrade_quality",
  "request_id": "string"
}
Header: X-Model-Variant, X-Fallback-Reason, X-Request-Id.

Li: also suggest a documented enum for fallback_reason so integrators can implement deterministic handling.

Raj: ops questions — rollout: propose canary 5% for 24h with automated gates: error_rate delta > 0.5pp, eval-suite quality drop > 3% absolute -> rollback. Require traceability in logs for variant selection and fallback events (request_id + variant + event_reason).

Sam: acceptance tests (proposal):
```
success_criteria = {
  "p50_latency_ms": "<=150",
  "error_rate_pct": "<=0.5",
  "eval_quality_drop_pct": "<3",
  "fallback_metadata_present": "100% when fallback occurs"
}
```
plus a CI job that runs customer-facing eval prompts against both pinned and fallback variants and fails the job on regression.

Anya: acceptance criteria (MVP):
- API returns model_variant, fallback_reason, and request_id on every response (fill with "none" or "n/a" when not applicable)
- When fallback occurs, response contains fallback_reason and X-Model-Variant header set to the actual variant used
- Canary recipe implemented with gating thresholds + automatic rollback trigger wired into deploy automation
- Perf tests added to CI (p50, p95, and error rate checks) and release blocked on passing
- Docs and a short playbook for SEs/CS with sample integration snippets and expected response examples

Li: non-goals reminder — no console UX for pinning or per-tenant toggles this iteration. We'll expose API-only hooks and iterate later.

Sam: engineering edge-cases to call out:
- KV cache / inflight cache when switching variants -> must either flush or map compatibility; we need an explicit strategy in the RFC.
- Tokenizer differences if fallback uses a different tokenization path -> require same tokenizer family for compatible fallbacks or include tokenizer id in metadata.
- Race conditions: simultaneous scale-up + fallback -> emit deterministic event order in logs and ensure requests include both chosen_variant and any later fallback event for audit.

Marta: customer comms — I'll draft the message to customers explaining the metadata fields, what a fallback looks like, and what to monitor. Request: sample integration snippet + expected response samples to include in the note.

Anya: owners: Sam (implementation + CI tests), Li (response metadata + docs examples), Raj (rollout automation + logging + alerts), Marta (customer comms + sample snippets). I'll own acceptance sign-off.

Sam: timeline ask — estimate ~2 sprints for a minimal API + CI + rollout automation MVP, assuming no infra blockers.

Raj: ops note — need a small schema PR in the ingest path to attach variant metadata; flagging infra review and potential schema migration.

Anya: next actions (owners + due dates):
- Sam: create RFC with endpoints + schema + cache strategy (due Wed)
- Li: mock sample responses + docs snippets (due Fri)
- Raj: outline rollout playbook + alerting thresholds (due Fri)
- Marta: draft customer note (due Mon)

Anya: please react with :thumbsup: when you agree with owners and timeline.
